newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks close down on political uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks close down on political uncertainties.

text.p: Political uncertainties in India's Congress party pushed down stocks in Delhi on selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and speculators, brokers said.
The benchmark Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE) index fell 6.14 points to 736.51.
Foreign Institutional Investors sold State Bank of India, Tisco and other blue chips, brokers said.

Senior party leaders were scheduled to meet later on Monday to elect a stop-gap succcessor to former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, who resigned as party chief on Saturday following a court summons to him in a cheating case in which he denies any involvement.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party coalition needs the support of Congress to survive in parliament.
Reports last week of defaults by two brokers in the country's premier stock exchange at Bombay also dampened trading sentiment, brokers said.
"The resignation of Rao as president of the Congress party might make the United Front unstable," said Vijay Aggarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services.
But other brokers said the uncertainty may give the coalition more breathing space.
Reliance Industries fell 2.20 rupees to 195.60 rupees while Tisco lost 3.25 rupees at 172.55 on selling by foreign funds, brokers said.
